record.question: The shear stress in turbulent flow is:
options: Linearly proportional to the velocity gradient
Proportional to the square of the velocity gradient
Dependent on the mean velocity of flow
Due to the exchange of energy between the molecules
record.explanation: In turbulent flow the shear stress arises from the exchange of momentum (energy) between fluid particles/molecules across layers, rather than being simply proportional to the velocity gradient as in laminar Newtonian flow.
